narrative:
Based on the information available, your loan application has been denied because the model assessed a 49% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. While that may sound like a coin flip, it is high enough that the bank considers you unlikely to repay the loan reliably.

The most important factors in this decision were, in order, the purpose of the loan, the balance in your checking account, and the amount you requested. The fact that you are buying a used car actually worked slightly in your favor—this is a common and generally less risky type of loan. But that positive influence was weak and not enough to overcome the other concerns.

A much stronger warning sign was your checking account balance, which falls between 0 and 200 DM. Among approved applicants, only about 18% had such a low balance; most had no checking account at all, which is treated as a neutral or better sign. Having very little money available suggests limited financial flexibility and makes it harder to handle unexpected expenses while repaying a loan.

The biggest concern, however, was the loan amount. You requested 7,966 DM, which is more than two and a half times the average amount approved applicants receive (about 3,020 DM). Larger loans carry more risk, especially when combined with a thin financial cushion.

To improve your chances next time, I recommend requesting a smaller loan or saving up a larger down payment so you need to borrow less. Keeping a healthier checking account balance and working on your credit history will also help. Consider waiting and reapplying with a stronger financial profile.
